thread:
marta: thinking out loud — what if the gateway supported an explicit prefetch / prewarm intent so edge can warm upstream conns and K/V caches for latency-sensitive short requests? e.g. client sends `x-rw-prefetch: true` and gateway maintains a short lease to finish prewarm before handing off. curious about tradeoffs.
kevin: +1 for reducing cold p99. two immediate concerns: (1) how do we avoid double-executing side-effects, (2) how does this interact with retries / hedging. need clear semantics.
sunil: side-effects are my main worry. we should limit prefetch to safe methods only (GET/HEAD) or an idempotency token explicitly provided. otherwise prefetch could trigger writes.
lara: we can do a two-phase handshake: client indicates `prefetch-intent` in headers, gateway responds with `lease-id` in 100-continue style, then does prewarm work under that lease; when client sends the actual request it references the `lease-id` so upstream knows this was a prewarm. that keeps prewarm from accidentally committing side-effects.
praveen: also need quota controls — prewarm amplification vector = attacker sends lots of `prefetch-intent` and we spin up expensive upstream work. propose server-side token bucket per-tenant and an adaptive scoring to reject heavy prefetches.
kevin: agree. also prefetch should be opt-in per-route. e.g. platform config `ingress.prefetch.enabled: [routes...]` and a max-concurrent-per-tenant. gate the feature.
ops-bot: experiment "ingress-prefetch-v1" deployed to canary (20%); metrics: +14% upstream connections during prewarm window, p50 latency for cold GETs -80ms.
marta: nice. @kevin @lara what about retries? if prewarm fails but client retries, we must avoid reapplying prewarm side-effects and not charge double. ideally prewarm is non-billable or discounted.
kevin: recommend prewarm be treated as a hint only — it should never be allowed to perform irreversible ops. Also mark prewarm requests with `X-Redwood-Prefetch: 1` and do not count them as billable tokens on hosted for now. For Dedicated customers we can surface opt-in billing.
sunil: on retry semantics: prewarm should be cancellable. if request gets retried upstream (hedge) the prewarm lease should be revoked for the losing attempt. make the lease TTL short (~500ms) and renew explicitly if client still wants it.
lara: propose a minimal wire sketch: client->gateway: `POST /path` with `x-rw-prefetch: true` -> gateway responds `103 Lease: id=abc123; ttl=500` then gateway does warm. when client sends payload it includes `x-rw-lease: abc123`. upstream receives `x-rw-prefetch-lease` and can decide to commit cached warm state or ignore. On streaming requests we can include trailer `prefetch-status: ok|miss|error`.
praveen: also need quota controls — prewarm amplification vector = attacker sends lots of `prefetch-intent` and we spin up expensive upstream work. propose server-side token bucket per-tenant and an adaptive scoring to reject heavy prefetches.
kevin: example header snippet: `x-rw-prefetch: true\nx-rw-prefetch-mode: kv+conn\nx-rw-lease-ttl-ms: 500`
kevin: config sample (yaml):
````
ingress:
  prefetch:
    enabled: true
    routes:
      - path_prefix: /v1/short
        methods: [GET]
    max_concurrent_per_tenant: 5
    lease_ttl_ms: 500
````
praveen: memory footprint: warming K/V caches will increase RAM in frontends or upstream. we should prefer warming upstream node-local caches rather than duplicating in the edge. otherwise we blow memory. also track metrics: prewarm_hit_rate, prewarm_cost_ms, prewarm_rejects.
marta: good list of metrics. for rollout I'm leaning to start with Dedicated customers and platform routes that are read-only. A/B via feature flag.
kevin: agree. Also add `prefetch-safety-level` in header: `safe|best-effort|aggressive`. default `safe`.
sunil: one more: retries + hedging. If a client sends two concurrent hedged requests and both used prewarm, we need deterministic ownership of warm state. easiest is lease binding: first arriving lease wins; others get `prefetch-status: joined|ignored`.
lara: and for streaming endpoints: if prewarm completes before stream open, gateway adds `prefetch-status: ok` to stream initial metadata; if prewarm in-progress, append `prefetch-status: warm-inflight` and emit trailer when done. helps the client adapt.
marta: action items: @kevin to draft RFC with handshake and header spec, @praveen to model cost amplification and quota proposal, @sunil to write the idempotency constraints section. i'll schedule follow-up eng-arch sync next Tue. thanks folks :thumbsup:
kevin: I'll open the RFC titled "ingress prefetch lease protocol" and include the YAML + header examples above. targeting review by EOW.
ops-bot: RFC created: https://rfc.internal/r/1234-ingress-prefetch-lease-protocol
marta: awesome — moving this to RFC review.
